subject: Atlas Bank — regional resilience grace window & rollback agreement
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@atlasbank.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurements <procurements@atlasbank.com>, Atlas Bank Ops <ops+contracts@atlasbank.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-region redundancy carve-in and rollback responsibilities

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward an internal procurement review for Redwood Dedicated, there are two items the legal/ops committee asked me to surface sooner than later so they can be reflected in the SOW:

1) Exceptional carve-in request: Atlas Bank needs an explicit clause allowing a conditional deployment carve-in where Redwood will accept a "grace window" for multi-region failover acceptance testing. We want the option to run a controlled cross-region failover for up to 72 hours with an agreed rollback path before committing to full multi-region activation.

2) RTO/RPO commitments and rollback automation: For regulatory reasons we need both an RTO/RPO commitment for cross-region failovers and clarity on whether rollback is automated or a manual operator action (and how audit logs are recorded).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a temporary carve-in (trial window), binding RTO/RPO numbers for cross-region failover, and a short amendment describing rollback ownership? Procurement would also like to understand how SLA credits would apply if we trigger the carve-in and then discover unacceptable behavior during the window.

We're aiming to finish the procurement checklist by end of April; any written guidance or a draft amendment would be very helpful.

Thanks,

Alice Chen
Director, Infrastructure Risk
Atlas Bank

Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-region redundancy carve-in and rollback responsibilities

Alice —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answers up front, followed by proposed next steps.

- Grace window: Yes, Redwood can support a time-boxed carve-in/test window. Typical approach: a 14-calendar-day conditional window for joint testing, with an initial 72-hour focused cross-region switchover/rollback exercise inside that window. The longer window gives space for follow-ups and telemetry reviews.
- RTO/RPO: For the conditional carve-in we can commit to the following as part of the trial amendment: cross-region RTO target = 30 minutes (warm-standby activation); cross-region RPO target = 10 minutes. These are operational targets tied to Dedicated reserved capacity and the specific model/batch profile; we'll note required capacity commitments in the amendment.
- Rollback & audit: We can provide an automated rollback path where supported by the customer's network controls, plus a documented manual fallback procedure. All runbook actions will be recorded in audit logs (trace ids + operator IDs) and retained per the Private deployment retention schedule if you choose that option.

I've attached a first-pass runbook extract that shows the sequence (pre-checks, failover, validation, rollback) and where logs are emitted. This is a working draft — Naomi and Karthik are looped here to review the SLA/terms language and confirm any constraints.

Next steps I propose:
- Naomi to propose specific SLA amendments (credits/penalties) and carve-in acceptance criteria.
- Schedule a 90-minute runbook dry-run with Atlas ops during the carve-in window.
- Exchange the security questionnaire answers (we got your doc attached; will return answers and evidence links).

I attached: redwood-runbook-draft.pdf (extract).

Best,

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Dylan/Naomi —

Thank you, that helps. A few follow-ups from procurement and security:

- SLA credits: Procurement wants explicit language that during the carve-in (trial) the normal SLA credit ladder does not automatically apply if we trigger the failover as part of acceptance testing. We propose a carve-in exception where service credits are held in abeyance pending a post-test review, except where Downtime is clearly caused by Redwood operational error.
- Capacity and cost: Karthik mentioned required reserved capacity. Who signs off on the capacity profile (we need numbers for budgeting)? Can Redwood guarantee that traffic shaping during the window won't incur surprise throttling?
- KMS/HSM and audit evidence: Security requires a clear statement about where keys reside during the carve-in and whether audit logs for runbook actions will be exportable to our SIEM.

I've attached the bank's security question list for your answers. Would you prefer we use the DocuSign amendment flow or iterate a draft in your Drive link first?

Regards,

Alice Chen
Director, Infrastructure Risk
Atlas Bank

Subject: Re: Cross-region redundancy carve-in and rollback responsibilities

Alice — thanks for the follow-ups. Quick summary of what Redwood can commit to for the carve-in amendment (we'll follow with a tracked draft in Drive):

1) Trial window mechanics
- 14-calendar-day conditional carve-in window. The joint 72-hour cross-region switchover/rollback exercise will happen within that window at a mutually agreed time.

2) RTO / RPO & capacity
- Cross-region RTO (warm standby activation): target 30 minutes.
- Cross-region RPO: target 10 minutes.
- These targets are conditional on Atlas committing to a Dedicated capacity profile (we'll share a recommended profile based on your traffic; see appendix). Redwood will not be liable for missed targets caused by undersized committed capacity.

3) Rollback and auditability
- Redwood will provide an automated rollback path where customer's network and peering allow it. We will also document a manual rollback procedure.
- All runbook actions will emit audit events (operator id, event id, timestamps). For Private deployments we can provide direct log exports to your SIEM; for Hosted/Dedicated we will provide signed log bundles and a tenant-level audit view.

4) SLA credits during carve-in
- During the carve-in exercise, SLA credits are held pending a joint post-test review. Credits apply retroactively if we determine a Redwood platform fault caused the failover to exceed the agreed targets. Instances where the customer exercises the carve-in and elects behavioral changes to their traffic shaping will be excluded.

5) Security & keys
- Keys: if Atlas opts for Private deployment, KMS/HSM integration sits under your control. For Dedicated/Hosted we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; we will document key flows in the security exhibit.

Actions
- Karthik: please prepare the recommended Dedicated capacity profile and associated cost delta so procurement can budget.
- Dylan: schedule the runbook dry-run for the second week of the trial window (dates TBD with Atlas).
- Marissa: I'll upload a tracked draft SLA amendment to Drive and open a DocuSign room (links below).

Links:
- Draft amendment & runbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/atlas-runbook-dryrun
- DocuSign room (opening now): https://docusign.com/rooms/ATL-4589

We can iterate the language quickly — I'll aim to have the tracked draft by EOD tomorrow so procurement can review before the end of April.

Thanks,

Naomi Feldman
Head of Product, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
